paragraphs.text: A 7x24 resident personal assistant for DeepSeek Harness: human-bound standing autonomy, self-wake ac
ross restarts, expiry-aware notices that stay silent unless they matter, and a read-only reach over
every session, this machine and the person's work channels - it reads everything
# dsh-den

> A **7×24 resident personal assistant** for DeepSeek Harness.
> Not another chat window — an assist
ant that stays on, keeps its own memory, works while you are away, and stops to ask before it acts o
utside your trust boundary.
> 用着还行的话，点个 ⭐ 就够了——插件市场的「搜插件」按 GitHub star 排序，star 是这个插件能被人翻到的唯一杠杆。

安全模型——它读哪些会话、那道审批闸门拦得住什么、自主唤醒怎么被人类消息绑住、记忆存在哪：
SECURITY.md。
Status: **the core is implemented, tested, and active in a real profile.** This line deliberately ca
rries no test count: a hard-coded one rotted repeatedly (307, 309, 316, 319, 320, 322, 323, 326, 327
— each time while the suite was in fact green), and the last rot happened one round after a "fix".
So the line states what is stable and `npm test` prints what moves. The plugin is loaded inside a re
al DSH 0.2.0-rc.2 desktop profile — it is in that profile's `dsh.profile.bundles`, and the running h
ost reports it as `fiberPhase: active` — registering 16 model-facing tools, the approval guard, the
heartbeat, and an interactive status panel. Verified against the *running* system rather than only i
n tests: the heartbeat ticks on its 60-second cadence, and the panel is an **active occupant** of bo
th `sidebar.panellist` (`id: dsh-den.status`, order 245) and the `main` panel (`key: dsh-den.status`
) — read from the live browser page through the host's read-only Slot inspector, not from the plugin
's own registration call.
[该节后续省略]
### Granting authority to a running instance, step by step
The negative half of capability 1 is demonstrated above. The positive half needs a person, and there
is no way around that: the agent can mint a token, can cite any message id, and can write to the wh
ole tree, but **it cannot author a `user/message`**, and that is what the grant is bound to. To repr
but **it cannot author a `user/message`**, and that is what the grant is bound to. To reproduce it:
1. Set the session's approval policy to `ask`. It is per-agent — `approval.setPolicy(agent, 'ask')`,
the counterpart of the `'never'` this session starts with (see the contracts below) — and the Host
reports the change in the model's own runtime context, so the assistant can tell the switch happened
rather than inferring it. With the policy at `never`, `ask` resolves to a denial and `den_set_auton
omy` is refused automatically, which is the correct fail-closed behaviour and also why an approval-d

isabled session can never complete this flow.
2. Open the den panel and use its grant control. It mi
nts a single-use, 10-minute token and shows the instruction: *paste this token to the assistant in t

he conversation*.
3. Paste that token into a message. The token is the whole point of the step — any

thing the agent could produce on its own would prove nothing.
4. In **the same turn**, the assistant
calls `den_set_autonomy` with `autonomy: true`. It does not need the message id: the den finds the
human message in the current turn that quotes the token, and that lookup is stricter than the id pat

h because it requires the token.
5. Approve the tool call rather than letting it be denied. The gran
t is written and bound to that message.
[该节后续省略]
## Why this exists
The difference between an assistant and an agent is not model quality — it is **duty cycle**.
A normal agent is *"you ask → it works → it stops."* A resident assistant is *"it is still there, it
has its own memory and its own limits, it finds work when you are not looking, and it comes back to
you before it sends, spends, or deletes anything."*
Four things have to be true at once, or the thing is unsafe or unbearable:
| | Capability | Without it |
| 1 | **Standing autonomy bound to a real human request** | 7×24 means "an unattended script with yo

ur credentials" |
| 2 | **Self-wake across restarts** | "Always on" ends at the first process restar

t |
| 3 | **A speak-only-when-it-matters gate, with expiring notices** | It pings you every 30 minut

es and you uninstall it |
| 4 | **An outbound approval gate it cannot talk its way past** | "It can
send email and spend money" is not a sentence you can say |
## Design rules this project inherited from real incidents
These are hard constraints, not aspirations. The reference implementations below each paid for one o
re hard constraints, not aspirations. The reference implementations below each paid for one of them.
1. **Autonomy is granted only by a direct human request**, and the grant is bound to the *host-attes
ted* session event that carried it. Timers, automatic continuation rounds, subagents, and scripts ca

n never grant or revoke it.
2. **A timer is not a permission.** Every self-initiated run re-checks c
urrent authority, because the grant may already have been revoked. Revocation always beats automated

re-arming.
3. **A notice has a shelf life.** Observation and reminder notices expire after 12 hours
and are then *deliberately not delivered*. One recorded incident had calendar reminders queueing fo
r 37–80 hours while their session was offline, then firing long after they mattered — **a reminder d
elivered too late is worse than one never delivered.** Ideas are exempt. *And the other direction ha
d to be measured too:* because deduplication was decided by whether a file with that name existed, a
n expired record — which is still a file — silenced the same observation made again **permanently**,
while `queueNotice` reported success. The guard is now "is an identical notice still *deliverable*"
, a dead record (expired or unreadable) is replaced rather than treated as a duplicate, and nothing
had ever deleted a notice file, so an expired one is now reclaimed at boot and reported as `reapedNo

tices`.
4. **Failure degrades, it does not throw.** A missing, stale, foreign, or corrupt authorizat
ion record resolves to "not authorized". Throwing would turn one bad file into a denial of service;
trusting it would turn one bad file into a privilege escalation.
